page.overview:
What is Lormark?

Lormark or Lower March or Northern Marshes (Polish: Dolna Marchia or Górne Aedirn) is a disputed region in Upper Aedirn. Located north of the river Dyfne, King Henselt of Kaedwen took it during the Nilfgaard-Kaedwen division of Aedirn early on in the Second Northern War with Nilfgaard. The Peace of Cintra, however, restored it to Aedirn.

The coat of arms in the infobox was designed by Artur 'Ruttou' Bagdasarian and based on the description in . The arms of Lormark is shared with Mansfeld family: Argent, a boar's head erased Gules.

This region's southern border was set by the Pontar river until , when the powerful Mansfeld family that lived in this region chose to invade their southern neighbor, Aedirn, and proclaimed the new southern border was now at the Dyfne river. Aedirn's king, Videmont, fought back and eventually drove the Mansfelds back across the Pontar. However, this conflict would end up causing the two kingdoms to have skirmishes for decades along this contested border.

Once a part of Kaedwen, the long disputed region, in late July , during the Second Northern War, was awarded to Henselt after the fall of Aedirn and his treaty with Emperor Emhyr var Emreis. The Dun Banner, along with five other brigades, were sent to occupy the region, and to meet Nilfgaard at the Dyfne should tensions sour.
